title: Weekly Engineering Standup
description: Fast-paced daily sync covering a flaky CI test, a dependency upgrade that broke staging, on-call handoff, and a quietly surfaced blocker.

summary.overview: The team moved quickly through a standup that surfaced two problems nobody had escalated yet: the test_payment_webhook_retry suite has been flaky for weeks and everyone had just been rerunning it instead of filing a ticket, so Alex volunteered to own the investigation while continuing his retry-path work. Tom reported that a Friday-afternoon Postgres client upgrade, merged as a minor version bump without a second reviewer, broke timestamp serialization and took staging's analytics service down; his fix pins the old serializer behavior and he agreed to add a changelog check requiring review on future minor bumps. Marcus handed the on-call pager to Priya for noon, flagging a known-noisy 3 a.m. disk alert, and near the end Alex quietly admitted he's been blocked since Monday on prod-read access to the analytics warehouse, which Marcus committed to escalating with IT immediately.

bullet_notes.title: Flaky CI test
points: test_payment_webhook_retry has failed repeatedly for weeks and people have just been rerunning it rather than filing a ticket.
Alex volunteers to investigate since he's already working in the webhook retry path for something else.
Marcus insists the ticket gets filed first, even if the fix lands within the hour, to have a paper trail on how long it sat.

bullet_notes.title: Dependency upgrade breaks staging
points: A Friday-afternoon Postgres client bump, merged as a minor version without a second reviewer, changed timestamp serialization.
Analytics service is fully down; the main app degrades but doesn't fully break.
Tom's fix pins the old serializer behavior and is in review; he'll also add a changelog check requiring a second reviewer on minor dependency bumps.

bullet_notes.title: On-call handoff and a quiet blocker
points: Marcus hands the pager to Priya at noon and flags the recurring 3 a.m. disk-usage alert as a known false alarm tied to log rotation.
Alex has been blocked since Monday on prod-read access to the analytics warehouse and hadn't raised it until asked directly.
Marcus commits to pinging IT right after standup to get the access approved today.

chapters.title: Round robin and Priya's updates
chapters.gist: Marcus opens standup and Priya reports shipping the billing retry fix before flagging that the webhook retry test failed again.

chapters.title: Nobody owns the flaky test
chapters.gist: Marcus admits no one has filed a ticket for the recurring failure and Alex volunteers to investigate it alongside his retry-path work.

chapters.title: Dependency upgrade breaks staging
chapters.gist: Tom explains how Friday's unreviewed Postgres client bump broke timestamp serialization and took down the analytics service, then proposes a fix and a bot policy change.

chapters.title: On-call handoff and a quiet blocker
chapters.gist: Marcus passes the pager to Priya, then Alex admits he's been stuck since Monday waiting on warehouse access that's now blocking the flaky-test work.

action_items.text: Ship the retry-logic fix for the billing webhook queue
File a ticket for the test_payment_webhook_retry flakiness and investigate the root cause
Land the timestamp-serializer patch pinning the Postgres client and confirm staging is green
Add a changelog / second-reviewer check to the dependency bot for minor version bumps
Get Alex's prod-read access to the analytics warehouse approved with IT

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Morning. Let's move fast, we're already running behind. Quick round robin — Priya, go ahead.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Yesterday I shipped the retry-logic fix for the billing webhook queue. Today I'm picking up signature validation on the same service.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Also, quick flag — test_payment_webhook_retry failed on my branch again. That's the fourth time this week.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Saw that fail on my PR yesterday too. Reran it, went green, moved on.

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: Same here. I've reran that test probably ten times in the last two weeks. At some point that's not a flaky test, that's a habit.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Has anyone actually opened a ticket for it, or are we all just quietly rerunning it forever?

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: ...No. Nobody has. That's on me, honestly, I keep meaning to and then standup ends and I forget.

segments.speaker: Alex Rivera
segments.text: I can take it. I was already digging into the webhook retry path for something else, might as well trace why it's flaky while I'm in there.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Take it. File the ticket first though, even if you fix it in the next hour — I want a paper trail on how long this sat.

segments.speaker: Alex Rivera
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Tom, you're up. What's going on with staging?

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: So, staging's been broken since last night. I upgraded the Postgres client library to pick up the connection-pooling fix, and it turns out the new version changed how it serializes timestamps.

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: Anything with a timezone-aware column started throwing on write. Analytics service is down hard, the main app degrades but doesn't fully break.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Wait, when did that merge? I don't remember seeing that PR.

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: Friday afternoon. It was tagged as a minor version bump so it didn't need a second reviewer. In hindsight that was the wrong call.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Friday deploy, nobody around over the weekend to notice — classic.

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: Yeah. I've got a patch pinning the timestamp serializer back to the old behavior, it's in review now. Should be in staging within the hour.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Okay. Can you also add a changelog check to the dependency bot so minor bumps on that package need a second reviewer going forward?

segments.speaker: Tom Whitfield
segments.text: Yep, I'll do that after the patch lands.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Good. Last thing — on-call. I'm handing it off to Priya at noon today, so heads up.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Got it. Anything still smoldering from your week I should know about before you hand me the pager?

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Just the payment retry flakiness, which Alex has now, and one alert that fires around 3 a.m. for disk usage on the log volume that's actually fine, it just crosses the threshold during log rotation.

segments.speaker: Priya Nair
segments.text: Noted, I'll snooze that alert's threshold instead of getting paged for nothing at 3 a.m.

segments.speaker: Alex Rivera
segments.text: Before we close — I'm actually stuck on something. I still don't have prod-read access to the analytics warehouse, I put in the request Monday and it's not showing as approved.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: That's been sitting since Monday? Why didn't you say something earlier.

segments.speaker: Alex Rivera
segments.text: Didn't want to make noise over an access request. But it's blocking the flaky-test investigation now since I need warehouse data to trace the webhook retries.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Noise is fine, that's what standup is for. I'll ping IT directly after this and get it approved today.

segments.speaker: Marcus Rodriguez
segments.text: Alright, that's the standup. Tom's patch, my on-call handoff to Priya, Alex's access ticket, and someone please actually file that flaky-test bug. Talk tomorrow.
